title: Bonsai shortcuts: small, safe operator actionlets + runbook-as-task SDK
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Oncall engineers frequently need to run small, repeatable operational actions (rotate a token, clear a KV cache shard, promote a canary route) but the existing runbooks are heavy and require a full runbook orchestration flow. This leads to either hand-crafted shell scripts (risky) or long ticketed interventions.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight "Bonsai Shortcuts" system: a library of tiny, composable operator actionlets that can be executed from the operator CLI or surfaced as runbook tasks in the runbook-as-tasks orchestration. Actionlets are:
- small (single-purpose), parameterized, and idempotent-by-default
- sandboxed by RBAC scope and optional approval gates
- annotated with automatic telemetry and structured outcome payloads so they can feed into the Console's remediation timeline

Deliverables for this ticket:
1) runbook-as-task SDK: a stable TypeScript/Go SDK to wrap existing ops endpoints into actionlets and produce a task manifest (inputs, outputs, dry-run implementation).
2) CLI integration: add `ops bonsai run <actionlet>` with --dry-run, --confirm, and --explain flags; integrate permission checks via token scopes.
3) Safety features: built-in circuit-breaker for high-risk actions, automatic pre-checks (quorum: service healthy, no competing deployments), and optional two-person approval for high-impact actionlets.
4) Telemetry/observability: standard metrics (attempts, success/failure, latency), structured logs to tracing, and a Console view for action history attached to incidents.

Non-goals: full workflow orchestration (that's for runbook engine); this focuses on small ops utilities that are safe to run interactively or as inline runbook tasks.

Why different from existing runbook work: Many runbook projects assume large multi-step flows. Bonsai prioritizes single-step, fast-response actions with stronger idempotency and safety ergonomics for oncall.
updates: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff meeting with SRE and DEX. Agreed scope: 25 actionlets MVP + SDK primitives. Action owners assigned for token rotate, cache flush, promote-canary, rollback-traffic.
2026-02-25 — Prototype: simple TS SDK that wraps existing /admin API endpoints and emits a task manifest. Built dry-run mode for 'kv:flush-shard'. Demo link added to Confluence (see links).

2026-03-01 — Security review prep: enumerated permission scopes required by common actionlets. Decided to implement least-privilege tokens per-actionlet and a two-tier approval for high-priv actions. PRD updated.

2026-03-04 — Design feedback from Product (Priya Menon): surface recent action results inline in the incident timeline; also make --explain produce human-readable pre-checks. Added to scope as low-effort UX changes.

2026-03-07 — Trade-off discussion: synchronous versus async execution. Chose async with streaming progress updates to Console to avoid CLI timeouts; CLI will poll task status and stream logs for UX parity.
2026-03-09 — Security review requested (see links). Implemented the circuit-breaker module and a feature-flagged approval flow for canary promotions.

2026-03-10 — Engineering review: core SDK API stabilized, integration tests for idempotency added. TODO: write 25 actionlet specs and add documentation to quickstart playbook. Planning follow-up spike for auto-rollback hooks if downstream errors detected.
